subject: Biology
description: CNS, PNS, neuron structure, synapse, reflex, brain regions

questions.stem: The CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) consists of:

options.option_text: Brain and ALL nerves of the body
Spinal cord and major arteries also
Brain, eyes, and ears as one system

questions.explanation: CNS = BRAIN + SPINAL CORD. Houses thinking, decision, central reflex circuits. Protected by skull + vertebral column + meninges + cerebrospinal fluid. PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (PNS) = nerves outside CNS. PNS branches: SOMATIC (voluntary muscles); AUTONOMIC (involuntary — heart, gut, glands), which has SYMPATHETIC ('fight or flight') + PARASYMPATHETIC ('rest + digest') divisions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The basic functional unit of the nervous system is:
questions.explanation: NEURON (nerve cell) — basic structural + functional unit of NS. Parts: (1) DENDRITES — receive signals; (2) CELL BODY (soma) — contains nucleus; (3) AXON — long projection that transmits signal to next neuron / muscle / gland; (4) AXON TERMINALS / SYNAPTIC KNOBS — release neurotransmitters at synapse. SYNAPSE = junction between two neurons (or neuron + target). Adult human brain has ~86 BILLION neurons, ~10¹⁴-10¹⁵ synapses. Distractor 1 = subatomic particle. Distractor 3 = kidney. Distractor 4 = part of cell.

questions.stem: REFLEX ACTIONS (knee jerk, hand pulling away from hot object) are controlled by:
questions.explanation: REFLEX ACTIONS — rapid, involuntary responses bypassing brain (or via brainstem). Pathway: stimulus → SENSORY neuron → SPINAL CORD (interneuron) → MOTOR neuron → muscle response. SPEED: ~50-150 ms (vs ~300+ ms if signal went to brain). Examples: KNEE JERK (patellar reflex — single synapse); withdrawal reflex (hand from hot); blinking; coughing; sneezing. Brain is INFORMED later (which is why you 'feel' the heat AFTER you've already pulled hand away). REFLEX ARC — a basic biology diagram.

questions.stem: Which part of the brain controls BALANCE + COORDINATION of voluntary muscles?
questions.explanation: CEREBELLUM ('little brain', at back-bottom of brain) — controls BALANCE, POSTURE, COORDINATION of fine movement, motor learning. Damage → ATAXIA (uncoordinated movement). CEREBRUM (largest part) — conscious thought, memory, sensory + motor (lobes: frontal, parietal, occipital, temporal). MEDULLA (oblongata) — automatic functions: breathing, heart rate, BP, swallowing. PONS — relays + sleep. MIDBRAIN — eye movements, hearing relay. HYPOTHALAMUS — temperature, hunger, thirst, hormones (controls pituitary). PITUITARY = endocrine gland (in skull, controlled by hypothalamus).

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter is associated with the 'reward' / 'pleasure' brain pathway?
questions.explanation: DOPAMINE — neurotransmitter in REWARD PATHWAY (mesolimbic system, particularly nucleus accumbens). Released for pleasurable activities (food, sex, music, drugs). DRUGS like cocaine, nicotine, amphetamines hijack this system → addiction. Dopamine deficiency → PARKINSON'S disease (tremor, rigidity, slow movement); excess in some pathways linked to schizophrenia. Other NTs: ACETYLCHOLINE (at neuromuscular junction; brain learning/memory; loss → Alzheimer's); GLUTAMATE (main excitatory); GABA (main inhibitory); SEROTONIN ('mood' — antidepressants are SSRIs); NORADRENALINE (alertness); ENDORPHINS (pain relief, exercise high).

questions.stem: MYELIN SHEATH wrapped around axons in the nervous system functions to:
questions.explanation: MYELIN SHEATH — fatty insulating layer around AXONS, formed by SCHWANN cells (PNS) or OLIGODENDROCYTES (CNS). Has gaps every ~1 mm: NODES OF RANVIER. Allows SALTATORY conduction — nerve impulse 'jumps' from node to node, much faster than continuous (up to ~120 m/s for myelinated, ~1-2 m/s for unmyelinated). Diseases: MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS (autoimmune attack on myelin in CNS); GUILLAIN-BARRÉ syndrome (PNS demyelination, often after infection). ALSO myelin makes 'WHITE MATTER' (vs gray matter = cell bodies + dendrites).

questions.stem: Which cranial nerve is the LONGEST + most extensive?
questions.explanation: 12 PAIRS of cranial nerves (numbered I to XII): I OLFACTORY (smell); II OPTIC (vision); III OCULOMOTOR (eye motion); IV TROCHLEAR; V TRIGEMINAL (face sensation, chewing); VI ABDUCENS; VII FACIAL (taste, expression); VIII VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR (hearing, balance); IX GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL (taste, swallow); X VAGUS (longest! — heart, lungs, gut, vocal cords; both sensory + motor); XI ACCESSORY (neck muscles); XII HYPOGLOSSAL (tongue). VAGUS = wandering nerve (vagus = wandering); important for the parasympathetic nervous system; vagus stimulation used to treat depression + epilepsy.
